findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer share deny entries
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from the raw `checkReq.UserUID` and never includes the identity type. Both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` parse to UID "0", so they get the same denial key.

The renderer is supposed to be able to read every dashboard and folder. Suppose an anonymous Check is denied for some dashboard. That denial is cached, and for the next 30s a renderer Check for the same action and dashboard returns the cached deny without ever reaching `getRendererPermissions`. Dashboard rendering then fails intermittently.

The same risk applies to any identity types whose raw UIDs overlap. Include the identity type, or the resolved identifier, in the key.

findings.title: Ambiguous `_` separator lets denial keys for different resources collide
findings.body:
The denial key joins name and parent folder with `_`, and Grafana UIDs commonly contain underscores. For example, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") both produce `...action_a_b_c`. Action and user UID are joined the same way.

A denial cached for one resource can therefore wrongly deny access to a different resource for the TTL. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or encode or length-prefix each component.

findings.title: Caching a denial reintroduces the stale-access problem for newly created resources
findings.body:
A denial is now cached for 30s right after a fresh DB lookup returns not-allowed. On later calls the denial-cache check at the top of Check returns early, so the DB is not re-queried.

If any Check for a resource runs before its creator's permission rows are committed, the creator is locked out of the new resource for the full TTL. Examples are the apiserver reading back the object during or right after create, or a UI poll. Likewise, permissions granted to a user right after a denial are ignored for 30s.

This is exactly the scenario the PR is meant to fix. Consider a much shorter TTL for denials, invalidating denial entries when permissions or resources change, or not caching denials for named resources.

findings.title: User identifier lookup is repeated on failure
findings.body:
`getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `GetUserIdentifiers`, which falls through to the DB on a cache miss. If that call errors, the error is swallowed and `getIdentityPermissions` immediately calls `GetUserIdentifiers` again, issuing a second identical DB query.

The same happens in List. It is wasted load in the error path, for example when a user is not found.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not prove the deny entry short-circuits the check
findings.body:
The comment says the permCache entry allows access "to prove this is not checked". But the entry is `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, and `checkPermission` treats a false value as no grant.

The Check would also fall through to the DB via the default `fakeStore`, which has no permissions. The request would be denied even without the denial cache, so the test passes regardless of whether the denial cache works. Set the value to `true` so the test actually checks precedence.

findings.title: Remote/cloud client keeps a 30s client-side cache, so the creator issue persists there
findings.body:
Only the in-proc client switches to `NoopCache`. In cloud mode, `newRemoteRBACClient` still caches Check results client-side for 30s.

The server-side re-query on a missing scope never runs for a decision the client already cached. A creator in cloud mode can still be denied access to a dashboard or folder they just created.
